label: H.R. 9604
title: Less Bureaucracy, Better Tribal Education Act

items.snippet: This bill transfers specified functions relating to tribal education and job training from the Department of Education (ED) to the Department of the Interior.
This bill transfers specified functions relating to tribal education and job training from the Department of Education (ED) to the Department of the Interior.
The bill outlines the authority of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) related to the functions that are transferred under this bill, including that OMB must ensure that this bill…

…bill, including that OMB must ensure that this bill does not create a net increase in full-time equivalent employees at Interior or ED. OMB must certify compliance with the bill to specified congressional committees.
The bill takes effect one year after ED corresponds with and publishes a response to Indian tribes on the bill's implementation.

lobbying.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.
lobbying.amount_note: Amounts are the income or expenses reported on the whole LD-2 filing, not money spent on this bill.

caption: This shows who the bill names and who lobbied on it. It does not show who gains or loses, and lobbying can be for or against a bill.

O000086.label: Overlap, not proof of influence.
O000086.caption: Money from this member's itemized individual donors (over $200) whose self-reported employer falls in an industry that also has a client lobbying on this bill. Correlation only; not a quid pro quo. Donors give to campaigns for many reasons, and a lobbying client may have opposed the bill.
O000086.note: None of this member's itemized donors work in the industries of this bill's lobbying clients.
